newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India receives 17 offers to supply LNG; GAIL chief.
newsitem.headline: India receives 17 offers to supply LNG; GAIL chief.

text.p: State-owned Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL), Indian Oil Corp (IOC) and Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) have received proposals from 17 companies to supply liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports, GAIL Chairman and Managing Director CR Prasad said on Monday.
Speaking at a gas for power generation conference in Singapore, Prasad said initiatives have been taken for the import of gas to meet rising demand coupled with its limited availability.

Indian demand for natural gas is expected to grow from 45 million cubic metres per day last year to around 150 million cubic metres per day by 2000, while production was projected to plateau at 68 million cubic metres per day by 2000.
To help meet the rising demand GAIL and partners IOC and ONGC are planning to set up import terminals for LNG. They plan terminals to handle five million tonnes of LNG per year.
"For the import of LNG, we have asked for bids and 17 companies, inluding Total, Shell, Mobil and British Gas, have quoted and are willing to supply," Prasad told Reuters on the sidelines of the

He said more than one other joint-venture partner might be selected from this shortlist, but a decision will not be made for about six month, when they also expect the government to give the go ahead for the project.
"We have already made the necessary proposal which is with the Government now and it is in its final stage for clearance," Prasad said.
The state companies will hold 50 percent of the import venture, and the remaining stake will be divided among LNG suppliers or producers and the Indian public, he said.

Prasad said two ports, Mangalore on the west coast and Ennore on the east have been identified as possible sites for setting two 2.5 million tonne-per-year terminals which would need investment of Rs 16,000 crores ($4.46 billion).
He added financing was not a problem for the cash-rich state-owned companies.
"Money is not going to be any problem," he said. ($1=Rs35.90)
